questions.q: What method does Drucker recommend for discovering your strengths?
a: Record your expected outcome for key decisions and compare it a year later
Ask colleagues to rank you on a list of common skills
Take a personality test and follow its career suggestions
Reflect on the tasks you enjoyed most as a child
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes feedback analysis: note what you expect, then compare it with what actually happened.

questions.q: What does the summary advise if a job conflicts with your core values?
a: Avoid it, because the mismatch will hurt your performance and judgment
Accept it and try to change your values over time
Stay only if the salary is unusually high
Keep your beliefs private and focus on the work
questions.why: Lesson 1 warns against working for a mission that contradicts your beliefs, since it affects performance and your moral compass.

questions.q: What should you communicate to others to improve how you work together?
a: Your expectations, values, boundaries and preferred work style
Only the tasks you are willing to accept from them
Your career ambitions and salary expectations
Feedback about their weaknesses and mistakes
questions.why: Lesson 2 says stating your expectations, values, boundaries and style strengthens communication.

questions.q: What risk does the summary associate with focusing only on one career?
a: Burnout or a midlife crisis when the work stops feeling meaningful
Losing technical skills as the industry changes
Earning less than people with several careers
Being passed over for leadership positions
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes people who reach the top, feel their work is meaningless and end up burnt out.

questions.q: Which approach to a second career does the summary mention?
a: Building it alongside your existing job when time allows
Quitting your first career before planning the second
Waiting until retirement to start any new work
Choosing a second career identical to the first
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists starting it, developing it alongside the current job, or starting a nonprofit or community role.
